title: One domain per package
statement: Every Go package under internal MUST hold only files that the technical records of one domain name, besides the product's shared value types and the shared generator interface in internal/gen, which belong to no domain; a package whose files two domains name MUST be split, one package per domain. A cmd package composes domains: it is named by their CLI handler records and belongs to no one domain, as ST-STD-CODE-R03 already lets it import any.

title: The code is named as the record names it
statement: A technical record of a kind whose title Lathe defines as the name in code (a handler, a CLI handler, predicate, service, adapter, value type, event type, data model, projection, reader, repository or rule), or a table, MUST have as its title the package-qualified identifier its file declares, such as assure.Decision, and that identifier MUST be declared in the file the record names; a record whose identifier the file does not declare is not built. A CLI command, an entry point and a generator keep the title their own kind defines: the invocation, the binary name and the template path.

title: Imports follow the domain order
statement: A package of one domain MUST import a package of another domain only along the order: Assuring and Declaring import no other domain; Supplying imports Declaring; Generating imports Declaring and Supplying; Extending imports Declaring and Generating; Building imports Generating; Distributing and Delivering import Building. A cmd package MAY import any domain; shared value types, the shared generator interface in internal/gen and the standard library belong to no domain.

title: A test names what it proves
statement: Every test function or subtest that proves a test record MUST carry that record's ID in its name, and every test file MUST carry at least one test record's ID; a test file that names no record proves nothing.

title: No source file without a record
statement: Every source file under internal, cmd, scripts and registry MUST be named by a technical record, directly or through a folder the record names; a change that adds a file no record names MUST add its record in the same change or not add the file.

title: A stub is not built
statement: A function that a predicate, handler or service record names MUST read its inputs; a function whose body only returns constants, or only panics, MUST NOT count as built, and assure gate change MUST refuse a change that adds one.

title: A wrapper counts only the subtest it names
statement: A test that runs other tests, such as the tests of a generated service, and reads their outcomes MUST count, for each test record, the outcome of the subtest that carries the record's ID itself; it MUST NOT count the pass of a subtest under that subtest, whose name has the same prefix, as its pass.

title: The user docs are the docs on the inventory
statement: The user docs MUST be exactly the Markdown files that the user doc inventory (ST-ASR-TOOL05) lists, README.md first, and each file it lists MUST be in the tree. No rule of this standard MUST ask for a doc that is not on the inventory; a change that writes a new user doc puts it on the inventory.

title: What a user doc names exists
statement: Each stego command line that a user doc gives in a code block or an inline code span MUST be a CLI command record that a handler file in the tree runs, with only the flags that its usage lists; each relative link of a user doc MUST name a file or a folder of the tree; and each code block of a user doc that is a whole service declaration (its first line is kind: service) MUST pass stego validate against the repository's registry.

title: Generated sections are what the spec gives
statement: A section of a user doc between the markers <!-- stego:generated <name> --> and <!-- stego:end --> MUST be exactly what the generator of that name gives from the spec and the tree at the same commit; the generator cli-commands gives the table of the built stego commands with their usage. go test ./internal/assure -run TestOwnTree -update-docs writes the sections again.

title: A doc changes with the command it names
statement: The change gate MUST refuse a change that alters the usage or the description of a CLI command record, or removes the record, when a user doc names that command outside a generated section at the base and the change leaves that doc as it is.

title: A generator does no I/O
statement: A generator MUST NOT read or write files, use the network or start a process. It MUST work only from the context the compiler gives it.

title: A generator reads no clock, environment or randomness
statement: A generator MUST NOT read the clock, the environment or a source of randomness.

title: A generator's output does not depend on map order
statement: A generator MUST return its files, and write their content, in an order that does not depend on the iteration order of a Go map.

title: A test of an obligation runs on a workstation
statement: Each automated test of an obligation MUST run on a developer's workstation with only local, unprivileged services: containers without privilege and local processes. It MUST NOT need a shared cluster or a hosted service.

title: One documented command runs each suite
statement: Each test suite MUST run from one documented command on a developer's workstation.

title: An outside system has a local stand-in
statement: A test that needs an outside system, such as a hosted CI provider, Konflux, Argo CD, an OCI registry, an identity provider or a signer, MUST run against a local stand-in that keeps the same contract. A test against the real system MAY exist in addition, but never in place of the test against the stand-in.

title: The suite starts each local service at a pinned version
statement: A local service that a test needs MUST be started by the test or by its suite, at a pinned version.

title: A test leaves no state outside a temporary folder
statement: A test and each local service that it starts MUST leave no state outside a temporary folder when the test ends. A cache of pinned images and tools that is keyed by digest is not state.

title: A cluster test is never the only proof
statement: A performance, stress or scale test MAY need a shared cluster, as AGENTS.md says. Such a test MUST NOT be the only proof of an obligation.

title: No record relies on the debug hatch
statement: A guarantee, a test record, an output contract and a business outcome measure of a generated service's signals MUST NOT rely on the output of log or log/slog, or on what a service writes to standard error; a record that needs a service signal MUST name a declared observation or a built-in observation of ST-SUP-RP12-LC21. A command-line program's diagnostics on standard error, such as those of ST-SUP-RC04-OC30, are not service signals, and this rule does not cover them.

title: A local run turns the console sink on
statement: Each local run of a generated service, in a test that runs under ST-STD-LOCAL or on a developer's workstation by the documented steps, MUST set STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE to json or logfmt, so its signals show on standard output without a collector.

title: A deployment does not turn the console sink on by default
statement: The Kubernetes base and the GitOps deployment objects that STEGO writes (ST-DLV-UC07) MUST NOT set STEGO_PROBE_CONSOLE, so domain observations stay off the console in each environment that its own overlay does not turn them on in; the built-in service events are on the console in every environment (ST-SUP-RP12-LC22).

title: The library is not a framework
statement: The runtime library MUST expose functions and types only. It MUST NOT scan, discover or register anything by name, struct tag or init(), and MUST NOT call into a service except through a value the service's own code passed it.

title: No reflection, no unsafe
statement: The runtime library MUST NOT import reflect or unsafe; where encoding needs reflection, it MUST go through the standard library at the service's own call.

title: A breaking change is a new major module
statement: The library's API MUST stay compatible within a major version, checked by apidiff in the common registry's CI, and a breaking change MUST ship as a new major module path.

title: One module, released with the common registry
statement: The runtime library MUST be one Go module with one package per concern, tagged and released with the common registry, so one pin names it.

title: Static code lives here
statement: Code that is the same for every declaration MUST live in the runtime library and MUST NOT be emitted by a generator; code that varies with the declaration MUST be generated and MUST NOT be interpreted by the library at run time.

title: One transaction type from database/sql
statement: The runtime library MUST take a store transaction at each package boundary as *sql.Tx of database/sql, as an interface of the package that *sql.Tx satisfies, or through a thin exported adapter from *sql.Tx; it MUST NOT import a database driver outside its test files, except in the one connector package github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime/pgconn, which holds the tenant runtime's connector and session guard and the outbox Listener adapter; and its tests MUST reach PostgreSQL through pgx's database/sql driver, so the command handle can pass one transaction to every runtime package. The listener session MUST use a direct DSN, not one behind a transaction-mode pooler, because LISTEN does not work behind one.

title: One signed compiler holds every generator
statement: STEGO MUST ship as one signed artifact that contains every generator it can run.

title: The compiler runs no generator code it does not contain
statement: The compiler MUST NOT load, download or execute generator code that its signed artifact does not already contain.

title: Outbound calls reach only named origins
statement: Generated code that sends a request to an outside system MUST send it only to an origin its configuration names, over TLS with an explicit CA bundle and no ambient credential, and MUST refuse a response larger than its stated limit.

title: A pulled artifact is verified before use
statement: Code that pulls an artifact MUST check it against the digest it asked for, or against the trusted signer the registry's ci-pipeline component names, before any other code reads it, and MUST refuse one that differs or that another identity signed.

title: Delivery to a GitOps tool writes files and applies nothing
statement: Code that delivers to a GitOps tool MUST write declarative files that the tool pulls from version control, and MUST NOT call the tool's API, hold its credential or apply a resource to a cluster.

title: A published event is a versioned record at a known address
statement: A published event's durable form MUST be a versioned record at a known address: the service's own generation state in its sources, the registry under version control, the CI provider's attestation store or an OCI referrer. The command that consumes the event MUST read that record at its next run, and STEGO MUST NOT depend on a relay or a running service to deliver it.

title: Two tenant controls that fail differently
statement: Every generated store method MUST take a tenant of the distinct Tenant type and add the tenant predicate, and every tenant-owned table MUST have row-level security enabled and forced with one policy on the transaction-local tenant setting; a zero tenant MUST be refused before any query, never treated as an empty filter. One tenant-owned table MAY have one more policy: the outbox queue table stego_outbox.messages has, beside its tenant policy, a relay policy for SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE, never INSERT, of the NOLOGIN outbox relay role of the service, <service role prefix>_outbox_relay, which owns the outbox relay functions and is reached only through them (ST-SUP-RP01-LC19); and the key table idempotency_keys MAY have, beside its tenant policy, a policy for SELECT and one for DELETE, never INSERT or UPDATE, of the NOLOGIN purge role of the service, <service role prefix>_idempotency_purge, which owns only its purge function and is reached only through it (ST-SUP-RP07-LC11); and no role of one service MAY connect to the database of another service, so neither policy of a NOLOGIN role is reachable from another service in the same cluster (ST-SUP-RC27-OC04). The orchestrator decided this under the Product owner's delegation (2026-11-11), in the recheck of PR #206 (finding F1), and made the outbox relay role one role of each service (ST-SUP-Q106, option a). Two tables are not tenant-owned, and no other table MAY be: the table authz_floor of the authorization runtime, which holds one token for the whole service and no tenant data, which every tenant's transaction reads, and which only the relay raises, in its own transaction that touches no tenant-owned table; and the tenant list stego_tenants of the tenant runtime (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07), which holds one row per tenant with its ID and its provision and retire times and no other tenant data, which the runtime role reads, and which the runtime role writes only through the owner's functions that Provision and Retire call, each in the transaction of the tenant it names. The audit tables are tenant-owned: each tenant has its own audit chain (ST-SUP-RP05-LC04).

title: The tenant setting is transaction-local
statement: The generated store code MUST set the tenant with set_config(name, value, true) at the start of every transaction and nothing MAY use a session-scoped SET, so a pooled connection never carries one tenant to the next client.

title: The runtime role owns nothing and bypasses nothing
statement: The database role a service runs as MUST NOT own any table, MUST NOT hold BYPASSRLS, and MUST hold only the privileges the generated code uses; migrations MUST run as the owner role in a separate job.

title: No tenant-less path from a request
statement: A worker or controller that touches more than one tenant MUST iterate tenants and open one transaction per tenant with that tenant set, with one exception: the outbox relay claim (ST-SUP-RP01-LC19) is the one statement that spans tenants, inside a relay function, and it returns each claimed message with its tenant, so every later step of that message runs in a transaction of the message's tenant; no code path reachable from a request MAY run without a tenant, and the tenant MUST come from a verified identity claim, never from a client-supplied header or body field.

title: The audit row commits with the change
statement: Every mutation of an audited entity MUST write its audit row in the same transaction as the change, and a denied or failed mutation MUST write its audit row with the outcome in its own short transaction, so there is no record without a change and no change without a record.

title: The audit table is append-only and copied out
statement: The runtime role MUST hold SELECT and INSERT only on the audit table, never UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE, a trigger MUST reject UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, and every audit row MUST also be enqueued in the outbox for the audit sink, keyed by the audit event id, so the sink is idempotent and the service cannot edit its own history. SELECT serves the entity history query (decision on ST-SUP-Q35).

title: A hash chain over redacted records, anchored outside
statement: Each audit row MUST carry prev_hash and hash over the canonical redacted record, fields declared pii MUST be redacted before hashing and fields declared secret MUST never be stored, and a periodic job MUST publish the chain head and row count to the sink, because a chain alone does not detect truncation.

title: Deny is a decision with a consistency floor
statement: Every authorization check MUST carry a consistency of at least the token stored on the resource row, a deny MUST be a decision and not an error, a list MUST be filtered to the resources the subject may see and an empty list MUST be 200, and the tenant predicate MUST be applied before any authorization filter.

title: System principals are subjects, never a bypass
statement: A worker, controller or relay MUST call the authorization port with its own service-account subject that the schema grants relations to; a bypass flag in a slot or a setting MUST be refused at generation.

title: Relationships are written only through the outbox
statement: A relationship tuple MUST be enqueued in the same transaction as the row it describes and written to the provider by the relay with idempotent touch and delete operations, in order per resource key, and the token the provider returns MUST be stored on the row; a handler MUST NOT write a tuple directly.

title: The idempotency record commits with the write
statement: An inbound idempotency key MUST be recorded in the same transaction as the write it guards, scoped by tenant, principal and key, with the fingerprint of method, path and body and the stored response; a 5xx response MUST NOT be stored, a concurrent duplicate MUST get 409 and a reused key with a different fingerprint MUST get 422, as the IETF Idempotency-Key header draft states.

title: Money is integer minor units with a currency
statement: A money amount MUST be an integer of minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code, a float MUST be refused at checking, and a ledger MUST hold one currency, so a cross-currency move is two transfers through a conversion account.

title: A ledger is append-only and balanced
statement: A transfer and its entries MUST be inserted in one statement that rejects an unbalanced set, posted entries MUST NOT be updated or deleted, a correction MUST be a new transfer that names the one it reverses, a pending transfer MUST be posted or voided by a new row and only once, and a balance MUST be derived from entries after the latest snapshot.

title: Rows are owned by the lock that claimed them
statement: Outbox and job rows MUST be claimed with SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and a handler MUST be idempotent or MUST be dispatched so that an unknown outcome is reconciled or parked and never sent again blindly, because the relay can crash after acting and before recording the fact; a session-scoped advisory lock MUST NOT be used, since it is orphaned behind a transaction pooler.

title: A controller holds a lease with a fencing token
statement: One controller instance MUST be active at a time, elected on a lease row whose renewal increments a fencing token, and every write the controller makes MUST carry that token and fail when the lease holds a higher one; on shutdown the holder MUST release the lease and flush its checkpoint. Where the provider behind a write cannot refuse a stale token, takeover MUST fail closed: the controller runs one replica, a lease that expires is not taken over, and an operator restarts the holder.

title: Modes are component sets in one binary
statement: A service MUST be one binary that runs the api, worker and controller modes selected by a repeatable flag, with all as the default, each mode with its own readiness and shutdown sequence; a mode MUST be a named component set and never a fixed bundle.

title: Declared invariants have one known emission
statement: A declared invariant MUST be one of unique in a scope, no overlap on a range, or sum limit under a parent, emitted as a unique index, an exclusion constraint, or a constraint trigger that locks the parent row; a rule with no such emission MUST stay a slot. Until a generator emits a declared invariant, generation MUST refuse it, naming the invariant, its kind and its entity, and write nothing, so a service never runs without a rule that checking accepted. The orchestrator decided this on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation.

title: Authorization covers every exposed operation, or the declaration is refused
statement: When a declaration binds an authorization provider, every entity a collection reads MUST declare a resource type and every operation of every collection MUST name a permission of that type, or public with a reason; checking MUST refuse an entity or an operation left out, naming each, and the emitted router MUST register a route only from the permission table, so a route without a decision cannot exist. The revocation status route that the provider's component adds is the one route whose decision is not a permission: it allows only the principal and tenant that made the write.

title: A statement names each table and function with its schema
statement: Each SQL statement of the runtime library and of the generated code of a service that the runtime role, the worker role or the relay role runs MUST name each table and each function of a schema manifest (ST-SUP-RP15-LC01) with its schema, and each login role of the service MUST have the search path public, pg_temp, because a name with no schema resolves in the first schema of the search path that holds it, and a relation or a function of the same name in an earlier schema, such as one named after the role, would stand in for it; a table with no row-level security would then give its rows to the role. The orchestrator decided the fix of S1 of the recheck of PR #243 on 2026-11-13 under the Product owner's delegation.
